title: Moral Framing and Ideological Bias of News
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the use of language related to the Purity/Sanctity moral foundation to quantify framing bias in news headlines. This foundation includes virtues and vices with religious connotations (e.g., church, sacred, pious, holy, impiety).
findings: The study found significant differences in how liberal and conservative media use language related to the Purity/Degradation moral foundation, which is strongly associated with religious concepts. Liberal media were found to stress this foundation more intensely, particularly emphasizing the violation of its vices (e.g., dirtiness, unholiness, impurity). In contrast, conservative media tended to emphasize the virtues of this foundation, such as austerity, sacredness, and purity.
